headline: Record backlog, raised guidance, margins dip on a tough comp
summary_short: Northrop Grumman's Q2 FY2026 sales rose 5.1% y/y to $10.876 billion and diluted EPS was $7.68 (vs $8.15 a year ago, which included a one-off divestiture gain), while net awards of $20.0 billion pushed backlog to a record $104.7 billion; the company raised full-year sales and MTM-adjusted EPS guidance.
summary_long: Sales grew 5% y/y and 10% q/q to $10.876B, driven by a 13% increase at Aeronautics Systems (B-21 and other restricted-program volume). Operating margin fell to 10.1% from 13.8% because Q2 2025 included a $231M divestiture gain, plus $61M lower segment operating income and a smaller FAS/CAS adjustment. Net earnings fell 7% to $1.094B ($7.68 diluted EPS), partly offset by a lower 6.3% effective tax rate (vs 17.7%) from IRS uncertain-tax-position remeasurement. Cash rose to $2.307B from $2.090B q/q; long-term debt was flat at $14.428B. Net awards of $20.0B lifted backlog to a record $104.7B. The company raised FY2026 sales guidance to $43.75-44.25B and MTM-adjusted EPS guidance to $28.60-29.10, reaffirming segment operating income and adjusted free cash flow guidance.

drivers.explanation: Higher sales at all four sectors; Aeronautics Systems led with a 13% increase driven by higher B-21/restricted-program volume, a $106M TACAMO ramp-up, and higher B-2/F-35/E-2 volume, partly offset by completed F/A-18 deliveries.
Not explained in the release — gross profit is not a management-discussed line item in this filing; the y/y decline tracks operating-cost growth outpacing the sales increase.
Primarily the prior-year $231M gain on the training-services divestiture, plus $61M lower segment operating income and a $56M smaller FAS/CAS operating adjustment.

The $329M operating-income decline was partly offset by a $179M lower tax expense (effective rate fell to 6.3% from 17.7% on IRS uncertain-tax-position remeasurement), a $29M larger pension benefit, and a $29M gain on an investment sale.
Not explained in the release — EBITDA is not a management-discussed line item; its decline follows the same operating-income dynamics noted above.
Reflects the net-income decline above, partly cushioned by a 1% reduction in weighted-average diluted shares from continued buybacks.

Net awards of $20.0B (led by $7.6B for Sentinel and $4.3B for restricted programs) lifted backlog to a company-record $104.7B; management raised FY2026 sales and MTM-adjusted EPS guidance citing demand and team confidence.
